name: streaming-response
title: Streaming Response
description: A model's response as it is written, that screen readers can follow: each finished sentence is spoken once, then how it ended.

examples.name: streaming-response-demo
examples.title: Streaming response
examples.description: A full reply: the writing shimmer, words that settle from the brand colour into the text colour, a glowing caret, and source chips once it finishes. Follows the brand's language.

examples.name: streaming-response-plain
examples.title: Plain text
examples.description: Ask, watch it write, and stop it part way, with no visual layer.

examples.name: streaming-response-states
examples.title: States
examples.description: Writing, stopped, failed and complete. The status line is words and a mark, never colour alone, and disappears once complete.

examples.name: streaming-response-status-only
examples.title: Speak only the start and end
examples.description: announce="status" for long answers people would rather read at their own pace.

props.name: status
props.description: Where the response is. The app owns it; the component never guesses from the text.

props.name: text
props.description: The response so far, as plain text. It is what screen readers hear, so leave out markdown symbols and code.

props.name: children
props.description: What sighted users see, such as rendered markdown. Defaults to text, with its line breaks kept.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the article, so it can be found by article navigation.

props.name: announce
props.description: sentences speaks each finished sentence as it arrives; status speaks only the start and the end.

props.name: announceInterval
props.description: Shortest gap between two spoken updates while streaming, in ms. Sentences that finish inside it are spoken together.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Shown and spoken after the error label when status is error.

props.name: text
props.description: The response so far. New words fade in from the brand text colour; a caret glows at the end while the parent streams.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the list of sources.

props.name: index
props.description: The citation number used in the text.

props.name: href
props.description: Where the source lives. Any React Aria Link prop works.

props.name: startLabel / writingLabel / completeLabel / stoppedLabel / errorLabel
props.description: Every spoken and shown word, for translation.

notes: The visible text is not a live region, so it is never re-read or chopped token by token. A separate polite live region, mounted with the component, speaks updates.
Sentences are split with Intl.Segmenter in the locale React Aria reports, so the Hindi danda and the Arabic question mark end sentences. Browsers without it announce at the end only.
A failed response's unfinished last sentence is not read out.
The status line pairs a mark with words; the writing dot's scale animation is off with reduced motion, its fade stays.
Not yet checked with a real screen reader. jsdom proves what is put in the live region, not what VoiceOver or NVDA say.

do: Pass plain text in text and the rendered version as children.
Set status to stopped or error when the stream ends early, so people hear that it did.
dont: Don't wrap it in another aria-live region; it already speaks.
Don't use it for text that isn't arriving progressively. Use Alert or Toast for a finished message.
